Explain how a VPN works in simple words
2:42 PM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and everything you send goes through it.

Normally, websites and your internet provider can see where your traffic comes from. With a VPN, your data is locked (encrypted) before it leaves your device, travels through the tunnel to the VPN company's computer, and only then goes out to the website. The website sees the VPN's address, not yours. Your internet provider sees only scrambled data going to the VPN.

It helps on public Wi-Fi and hides your location from websites. It doesn't make you invisible, though: the VPN company can see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
